## Overview

**Bardolemeu Romeo** is a 27-year-old human bard from one of the wealthiest and most influential families on the continent -- the Romeo family, owners of the largest and most prestigious theatres in the kingdom. Born into privilege, he rejected his inheritance at age 17 after discovering the exploitation and censorship that sustained his family's empire. He now wanders the land, bringing music and art to those who cannot afford it, carrying only his mentor Jilton's old lute and the lessons that shaped him.

---

## Appearance

A well-dressed human with the easy charm of a born performer. His clothes are fine but practical -- travelling clothes that once belonged in a wardrobe of luxury. He carries an old lute -- his mentor's instrument, worn from years of use -- and moves with the confidence of someone who has always had a stage, even if the stage has now changed.

---

## Background

Bardolemeu was born into the Romeo family, one of the richest and most influential houses in Kythoria. His family owns the largest and most prestigious theatres in the kingdom -- venues where nobles, merchants, and powerful figures gather for grand spectacles. From an early age, he was taught that art existed to generate profit, win favours, and strengthen the family's influence. Every play was chosen to please the powerful, every musician hired was a tool to maintain prestige, and every round of applause was measured in coin.

But Bardolemeu could never see music that way.

While his parents treated artists as servants and discussed revenue, contracts, and political alliances, he found comfort with an old musician who worked in one of the family's theatres. **Jilton Marboia** -- a thin man in his 50s with gray hair tied at the nape of his neck, green eyes, a short graying beard, slightly tan skin, and scars on his hands. He wore simple cream linen shirts and practical pants, nothing extravagant like a bard. Wrinkled not by age but by time itself. Despite everything, he carried a calm and almost whimsical presence.

Unlike everyone else, Jilton never treated Bardolemeu as an heir. He taught him to play the lute, to sing, and above all, taught him that true art belongs to the people -- not to the rich or the powerful. He often said that a good song could survive for centuries, long after any empire or fortune had crumbled. Jilton always wore a peculiar necklace or ring -- something he never explained, and Bardolemeu never deciphered its meaning.

As Bardolemeu grew older, he discovered the darker truths behind his family's prestige. Artists were exploited -- paid little for their talent and discarded when they were no longer profitable. Shows were censored to please the nobles. Stories were altered to protect influential figures. Anyone who dared to challenge the family's interests found their career destroyed. To his parents, art had no inherent value. It was merely a product.

Jilton knew too many secrets. He knew how artists were silenced, how plays disappeared on the orders of powerful people, and how fear was used to control those who depended on the family's theatres to survive. One day, he vanished without a trace. Bardolemeu was told he had left in search of new stages, but he never believed that lie. He is certain Jilton was silenced for knowing more than he should.

That same night -- the night of Jilton's disappearance -- Bardolemeu tried to play a song Jilton had been teaching him. Jilton had said it was one of his most important songs, but that Bardolemeu was not yet ready to learn it fully. Alone in the dark, Bardolemeu played what he knew -- and the lute played the last notes by itself. The instrument responded to him, completing the melody on its own. In that moment, Bardolemeu realised the lute was not just an instrument -- it was alive with magic, and it was answering him.

In that same moment, he also realised that if he stayed, he would become exactly like his parents.

He left the mansion that night without telling anyone. He took no jewellery, no gold, no part of the fortune that would one day be his. He took only Jilton's old lute and the lessons the man had left him. He made a promise to himself: he would never allow art to serve only those who already had everything.

The early days were hard. He went hungry, slept in the open, and discovered a world completely different from the one he was raised in. But it was also in this world that he found what Jilton had always tried to teach him. He saw a simple song unite strangers in a tavern, draw a smile from children who had never set foot in a theatre, and restore hope to people who had lost everything. He understood that music did not exist to feed the egos of the powerful or enrich those who exploited it -- it existed to inspire, to comfort, and to remind people that they are never truly alone.

Since then, he has wandered for ten years without a fixed destination. Every song he composes is a tribute to Jilton. Every story he tells seeks to immortalise the deeds of those who will never set foot on the stage of the great theatres. And every performance he offers freely to those who have nothing is a way of proving that art is worth more when it is shared than when it is sold.

## Family

- **Father**: Forte Romeo -- head of the Romeo family, theatre magnate
- **Mother**: Serena Romeo -- matriarch of the Romeo family
- **Sister**: Melodia Romeo (24 at campaign start)
- Bardolemeu's current relationship with his family is estranged and unresolved.

---

## Abilities

- **Bardic Magic**: Spells woven through music and performance
- **Bardic Inspiration**: Lifting spirits and empowering allies through art
- **Social Grace**: Raised in high society, comfortable in any gathering
- **Performance**: Singer, musician, storyteller, actor -- trained by Jilton
- **The Responding Lute**: Bardolemeu's mentor's lute is magically attuned to him. It played its master's unfinished song by itself on the night of Jilton's disappearance, marking Bardolemeu's bardic awakening. The instrument may hold further secrets tied to Jilton's unexplained necklace/ring.

---

## Goals

1. Bring the joy of music and art to those who cannot afford it -- honouring Jilton's teachings
2. Prove that art's true value lies in the lives it touches, not the wealth it generates
3. Experience the world firsthand, beyond the filtered lens of wealth and privilege
4. Understand his connection to magic through art (his bardic awakening -- the lute that responded to him)
5. Discover what happened to Jilton Marboia -- was he silenced? By whom? Is he still alive?
6. Decipher the meaning of Jilton's unexplained necklace or ring
7. Potentially return to his family's theatres -- not to reclaim his inheritance, but to open the curtains to all who were excluded

## Open Questions (for player input)

2. [question] **What specific secrets did Jilton know?** He knew about silenced artists, censored plays, and powerful figures pulling strings -- but was there something bigger? Did he know about the family's ViF ties?
3. [question] **What was Jilton's necklace/ring?** He always carried it. Bardolemeu never deciphered its meaning. Is it a key, a symbol, or a message?
